content.text:
I've found the cause, and it's a real bug, not something from this rung. I've stopped here.

**What happened.** `cycle --ladder` dropped `(done)` from rungs 0 and 1, and `cycle --status` now reports "0 on the branch" and says the next step is the opening.

**Why.** `branch_revset` (`src/cycle.rs:774`) takes the commits the cycle's bookmark reaches, minus those any *other* local bookmark reaches:

```
((::own | own::@-) ~ ::(bookmarks() ~ own))
```

The set-aside bookmark `aside-docs-rung` sits on a child of rung 1, so it reaches every commit of the cycle, and the subtraction empties the branch. Unplanned work tells us to set edits aside as a jj commit with a local bookmark, so following that rule breaks the tool.

**The fix.** Subtract only bookmarks that are not at or above the cycle's own:

```
((::own | own::@-) ~ ::(bookmarks() ~ own::))
```

`main` and older bookmarks still cut the branch off below. A bookmark at `own`'s own commit, such as `main` right after a fast-forward Land, is still excluded, exactly as today. A bookmark above the cycle, like a set-aside, no longer swallows it. This needs a test with a set-aside bookmark.

**Ways on**
1. **(Recommended) Insert another rung first, "fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole".** It's a separate defect with its own one-line problem, so a separate commit keeps the history honest. `--rung-start` follows it. Rung 1's commit is unaffected, since the bookmark didn't exist when it was made.
2. Fold the fix into the `--rung-start` rung, which means one rung fixing two unrelated things.
3. Work around it: delete the `aside-docs-rung` bookmark and address the set-aside commit by its change id `nruymrqm`, then fix it later as a Todo. That bends the rule that set-aside work gets a local bookmark.

Right now the working copy holds only the `TODO.md` record edits (the new rung heading and the plan) and the wrong ladder in `zTOC.md`. The next ladder write, once the fix is in, corrects `zTOC.md`.

The plain version: setting the docs edits aside with a bookmark, as the rules require, made the tool think the cycle had no commits. It's a one-line fix to how the branch is found, and I'd make it its own rung before `--rung-start`. Which way?

message.content: Is there a "set aside" a new command?

content.text:
No. There is no set-aside command. I did it by hand with four raw jj commands, following the Unplanned work rule ("a jj commit with a local bookmark, never a patch file"):

1. `jj restore --from @- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock`: kept the version bump out of the saved commit, so bringing it back won't conflict on the version line.
2. `jj commit -m "docs: the agent-files mark no rung current (set aside)"`: saved the edits.
3. `jj bookmark create aside-docs-rung -r @-`: gave the saved commit a local bookmark.
4. `jj new ruzplvtpntxt`: started a fresh working copy on rung 1.

Bringing the edits back will also be by hand: a `jj rebase` of `aside-docs-rung` onto the new tip, then deleting the bookmark.

That hand procedure is also what exposed the branch bug. The tool had never seen a set-aside bookmark because nothing in it makes one. That's a reasonable case for a command, so `vc-x1` owns the steps and their edge cases:
- one command saves the working copy as a set-aside commit with a local bookmark, leaves out the version files, and puts `@` back on the cycle's tip;
- a matching command rebases it back onto the new tip and deletes the bookmark.

Following the stage-flag naming, that might be `cycle --set-aside` and `cycle --take-back`.

I'd file it as a Todo rather than grow this cycle again, since it's outside the cycle's subject. It can go into `## Todo` in this rung's record edits before the commit. Should I add it?

The plain version: no, I set the edits aside with plain jj commands the rules describe. A command for it would make sense, and I suggest filing it as a Todo instead of adding it to this cycle.

content.text: If this is manual why code changes?

The code change isn't for setting aside. It fixes how `vc-x1` reads the repo, and the manual set-aside is what exposed the problem.

- **Setting aside** was plain jj, with no `vc-x1` involved.
- **`vc-x1` then reads the repo.** `cycle --ladder`, `--status`, `--commit`, and `--close` all work out which commits belong to the cycle, and they treat every other local bookmark as a boundary. The set-aside bookmark sits *above* the cycle's bookmark, so the tool cut away the cycle's whole history. The ladder lost every `(done)` and `--status` reported no commits.
- **So the bug is in the tool.** Any local bookmark above the cycle, made by hand or otherwise, does this. The rules themselves tell us to make one, so `--commit` would have refused or misread this cycle's next rung. The fix makes the tool ignore bookmarks above the cycle.

You have a choice about the fix, though. If you'd rather not change code for this now, the workaround from before still works: delete the `aside-docs-rung` bookmark, keep the saved commit by its change id `nruymrqm`, drop this rung, and file the bug as a Todo. That bends the Unplanned work rule, which asks for a bookmark. I'd still keep the fix: it's one line plus a test, and a future `cycle --set-aside` would need it anyway.

The plain version: setting the work aside was manual, but the bookmark it creates confused `vc-x1`'s count of the cycle's commits. The code change fixes that count, not the set-aside.

content.text:
The fix rung is committed, and its `zTOC.md` is correct (rungs 0 to 2 `(done)`). The fix itself is incomplete, though, and I've stopped before going further.

**What's wrong.** My fix covered a set-aside bookmark only while it sat *above* the cycle's bookmark, which is the moment of setting aside, and that's all the test checked. Once the cycle moves past it, the set-aside commit is a side branch forking from rung 1:

```
○  fix: a set-aside bookmark ...   ← cycle bookmark
│ ○  docs: ... (set aside)         ← aside-docs-rung
├─╯
○  fix: the ladder marks done rungs only
○  ... opening
```

The set-aside bookmark is no longer above the cycle's, so it cuts again. `--status` now counts 1 commit and warns about a done rung below unfinished ones. The next `--commit` would misread the cycle.

**What the fix needs to tell apart.** `main` is where the cycle *started from*, while a set-aside commit forks from *inside* the cycle. Bookmark position alone can't separate the two: after a sync, `main` can also sit beside the cycle rather than below it.

**Ways on**
1. **(Recommended) Cut only at bookmarks that don't descend from the cycle's opening commit.** The opening is the branch's first commit, and its title, `<cycle title> opening`, comes from the record. A set-aside forks after the opening, so it never cuts. `main` never descends from the opening, wherever a sync moved it, so it always cuts. A cycle with no opening commit yet falls back to today's rule. I'd amend the fix rung with this, through `vc-x1 squash`, plus a test of the side-branch case and of `main` moved by a sync. The rung is local, so squashing into it is allowed.
2. **Cut only at bookmarks that exist on a remote.** A set-aside is local-only, and `main` is tracked. This breaks for a workspace with no remote, or for another local cycle's bookmark.
3. **Bring the docs edits back now**, rebasing `aside-docs-rung` onto the tip and deleting the bookmark, so nothing forks. That unblocks this cycle without fixing the tool, and it would mean doing the docs rung before `--rung-start`, against the inserted order.

The plain version: my fix worked only while the set-aside commit sat directly above the cycle. Once the cycle moved on, it broke again. The robust rule is to ignore any bookmark that branches off after the cycle's opening commit. Which way?

content.text:
I agree it's brittle. I'd put the cause somewhere other than the file format, though: the markers are *worked out* from the repo graph instead of being *recorded*. Every `(done)` is recomputed each time by finding "the cycle's branch" with a revset, then matching commit titles against rung headings. Both steps are guesses about intent. A side branch, a moved `main`, a reworded title, or a squash can each throw them off, and today's two bugs are exactly that.

**What a structured file would change, and what it wouldn't**
- **Format alone:** a `zTOC.toml` read by serde instead of the hand-written markdown parser (`is_rung`) would be sturdier to parse and easy to extend. It wouldn't fix today's problem if the markers were still recomputed from the graph.
- **Format plus recorded state is the real win.** Each rung would carry its state and, once committed, its jj change id:

  ```toml
  [[rung]]
  title = "fix: the ladder marks done rungs only"
  state = "done"
  change = "ruzplvtpntxt"

  [[rung]]
  title = "feat: cycle --rung-start marks the rung in flight"
  state = "current"
  ```

  - `--commit` writes `done` and the change id because it just made that commit, so it doesn't have to infer it.
  - `--rung-start` writes `current`. Your earlier point falls out naturally: `current` becomes recorded state set when work begins, not a prediction.
  - The cycle's commits become the change ids it recorded, so `branch_revset` goes away. That removes its title matching and its bookmark rules, the commit counts, and the shape check at `--close`. Set-aside commits, other bookmarks, and moved `main`s stop mattering.
  - Drift is still detectable: a recorded change id that no longer resolves, or isn't an ancestor of the tip, is a clear finding. jj keeps change ids through rebase and rewording, so they're a much steadier key than titles.
  - More states become possible, like `dropped` for a dead-end's unstarted rungs, or the version each rung committed at.

**TOML over JSON.** It matches `.vc-config.md`'s blocks, allows comments, diffs line by line, and is pleasant to read by hand. JSON's only edge is tooling, and serde handles both.

**What it costs**
- **Clickable links.** The rationale for `zTOC.md` was a ladder you can click through in zed's preview. TOML loses that, unless `zTOC.md` becomes a generated view of `zTOC.toml`. A generated view doesn't drift the way two hand-kept copies did, but it's a second file in every commit. `cycle --status` might be enough of a view instead.
- **A second place for titles.** Rung titles would live in the TOML as well as the `TODO.md` headings, unless one becomes the source of truth. I'd keep the headings as the source and have the TOML record state against them. Then an inserted or renamed rung is still written once, and the tool flags mismatches.
- **Manual jj work can still make the record wrong,** for example abandoning a rung's commit. The difference is that it's detected by checking recorded change ids, not silently misread.
- **It touches the agent-files** (zTOC format, Cycle-record, the per-rung flow) and the `vc-dr-apply.sh` skeleton, so it's a proposal-sized change in its own right.

**Where that leaves this cycle.** If this is the direction, I wouldn't spend more on the revset fix. The simplest route is option 3: bring the docs edits back so nothing forks, finish the cycle as planned, and file "the ladder records its state" as the next cycle's Todo. That might also make `--rung-start` a rung of the redesign instead of this cycle.

The plain version: the fragility comes from the tool guessing which commits belong to the cycle, not from markdown. A TOML ladder that records each rung's state and commit id when the tool makes it would remove the guessing. TOML suits that better than JSON, and the main loss is the clickable markdown ladder, which a generated view could restore.

content.text:
I like it. It's the pattern `.vc-config.md` already uses, prose and links for people with TOML blocks for the tool, so the format is familiar and the code that reads concatenated TOML blocks from markdown already exists.

**What makes it work well**
- **The tool writes the link line too, not the agent.** If I typed the links, they'd be hand-kept copies of the block's title, which is the drift we just removed. Each block is the record, and the line above it is a view `cycle --ladder` and `--commit` regenerate from it. "No marker is typed" stays true for both.
- **Let the line carry the marker as well:**

  ````markdown
  - 2 (done) [fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole](TODO.md#fix-a-set-aside-bookmark-leaves-the-cycles-branch-whole)

  ```toml
  [[rung]]
  title = "fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole"
  state = "done"
  change = "wksprxupuxou"
  ```
  ````

  Reading down the lines still gives today's ladder at a glance and in the preview, and the blocks hold the data. `[[rung]]` makes the blocks concatenate into one array, in order, the same way `.vc-config.md`'s blocks combine.
- **Diffs say what happened.** A rung's commit shows `state = "done"` and its `change` id appear, and the line's marker flip beside them. `--rung-start` shows `state = "current"` in the working copy.
- **Per-rung blocks keep each rung's line and data together,** so inserting, dropping, or reordering a rung touches one pair, and merge conflicts stay local.
- **The landmark keeps more.** The closed ladder in the closing commit maps every rung to its change id, a durable record of which commit was which rung that holds even if titles are reworded.

**What it costs**
- **Length.** About six lines per rung instead of one, so a ten-rung ladder runs to about sixty lines. In zed's preview the fenced blocks will be visible and somewhat noisy.
  - A variant: the link lines as one list on top, with all the data in a single `[[rung]]` block below. That's more compact to read, but each rung's line and data are apart. Since the tool writes both, the separation can't drift, so it comes down to taste. I'd lean toward your per-rung form for the adjacency, unless the preview noise bothers you.
- **Hand edits get overwritten.** Anyone editing a line or block by hand loses it on the next write, unless the tool refuses a block that doesn't match the headings. It should refuse, naming the mismatch, as `--ladder` already does for a line that isn't a rung.
- **The headings in `TODO.md` stay the source of the titles.** The blocks record state against them, and the tool reports a heading with no block, or a block with no heading.

The plain version: one `zTOC.md` where each rung is a tool-written link line, with its marker, above a small TOML block of its state and commit id. That gives you clickable links and a glanceable ladder for people, and recorded state for the tool. The one rule that matters is that the tool writes both halves, so they can't drift.

**The subject grows.** The cycle stops being "drop `(current)`" and becomes "the ladder records its state": `vc-x1` owns `zTOC.md`, each rung is a tool-written link line above its own TOML block, and the cycle's commits are the change ids it records. The title "fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current" stays true but becomes narrow. Nothing is pushed, so a rename is still possible, to something like "feat: zTOC.md records each rung's state". That means re-describing the local opening commit and renaming the bookmark. Your call. Keeping the title is less churn.

**What happens to the rungs already made**
- **0, the opening, and 1, "the ladder marks done rungs only":** both stay. Rung 1's reader for the old line ladder, including `(current)`, becomes the migration reader that turns an old `zTOC.md` into the new form.
- **2, the set-aside fix:** this becomes moot rather than wrong. Once the ladder records change ids, `branch_revset` stops deciding which commits are the cycle's, along with the commit count, the shape check at `--close`, and the stray-commit refusal. I'd keep it, since it's a true step in the history, and note in its subsection that rung 5 below supersedes it. Reworking it away is also allowed while local, but that rewrites history for no real gain.

**The set-aside docs edits.** I'd drop them. The docs rung will rewrite those same five passages for the new format, so the saved edits would only conflict. Deleting `aside-docs-rung` also fixes the current tool's branch right away, so the next commits work with `vc-x1-dev` as it is. The saved commit can stay addressable by its change id `nruymrqm` as a reference until the docs rung is done, then be abandoned.

**The new ladder**
- 0 (done) opening
- 1 (done) fix: the ladder marks done rungs only
- 2 (done) fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole
- 3: **feat: zTOC.md holds a TOML block per rung.** The format, its reader and writer, and the refusal of a hand edit: any line or block that doesn't match what the tool would write is refused, naming the mismatch. The old line ladder is migrated. This rung's own commit converts this cycle's `zTOC.md`, recording change ids for rungs 0 to 2 by matching titles once.
- 4: **feat: cycle --rung-start marks the rung in flight.** This gets simpler: it writes `state = "current"` into the block.
- 5: **feat: the cycle's commits are the ladder's change ids.** `--commit` records `done` and the change id. `--status`, the shape check at `--close`, and the opening-or-rung decision read the record. A recorded change id that is no longer an ancestor of the tip is a finding. `branch_revset` retires, or is kept only for migration.
- 6: **docs: the agent-files describe the recorded ladder.** The zTOC format is rewritten, plus Cycle-record, the per-rung flow's new start step, the rationale, and the `vc-dr-apply.sh` skeleton, as `v0.3.1-14`.
- 7: closing.

**Other effects**
- **Dogfooding.** From rung 3's commit on, this cycle runs on the new format, committed by `vc-x1-dev`. Rungs 4 and 5 test themselves on the cycle that builds them, so the acceptance check can be stated against this cycle's own `zTOC.md`.

The plain version: the three commits already made stay, the set-aside docs edits get dropped, and four new rungs build the new `zTOC.md`, the `--rung-start` command, change ids as the cycle's commits, and the docs. From the format rung on, this cycle runs on its own new ladder.

content.text:
Yes, I think that's the cleaner model. `TODO.md` holds everything, and `zTOC.md` is just a view: regenerated by every `cycle` command, never edited by hand, and checked by regenerating and comparing, so a hand edit is a finding. Two refinements on what goes into `TODO.md`:

**1. Store the state, not "M (done)".**
- The number is the rung's position, which the tool can always compute. Stored numbers would need rewriting on every insert, the churn we just removed. `zTOC.md` shows the numbers, and `TODO.md` doesn't keep them.
- What `TODO.md` keeps is what can't be computed: the state (`current`, `done`, maybe later `dropped`) and, once done, the change id.

**2. Put it in a small TOML block under the rung heading, not in the heading.**
- A heading like `##### 2 (done) fix: x` changes its anchor whenever the state changes. That breaks every link to it, including `zTOC.md`'s, and every commit title would need the marker stripped before comparing.
- A block keeps the heading, and so the anchor and the commit title, stable:

  ````markdown
  ##### fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole

  ```toml
  state = "done"
  change = "wksprxupuxou"
  ```

  (found 2026-11-15, setting the docs rung's edits aside) The branch was ...
  ````

  Your per-rung TOML idea, moved to where the record lives.

**What follows from this**
- **Ownership is split cleanly within one file.** People own the headings and prose. The tool writes the blocks, through `--rung-start` (`current`) and `--commit` (`done` plus the change id), and checks them: a change id that doesn't resolve, or isn't an ancestor of the tip, is a finding. Your rule still holds: while a rung is unpushed, you can edit `TODO.md` directly, including a block, for example marking a rung `dropped`, and the tool rechecks it.
- **`current` never reaches history.** `--rung-start` writes it in the working copy and the commit turns it into `done`, as before.
- **The noise moves.** `zTOC.md` stays one line per rung, as clean as today. The cost is about four lines per rung inside the record in `TODO.md`, next to prose that already describes the rung. That may well feel less noisy than blocks in `zTOC.md`.
- **The landmark gets the full mapping.** Closing moves the block to `## Closed` with its state blocks, so the landmark's `TODO.md` holds which change id was which rung. `zTOC.md` in the same commit is just the regenerated view of it.
- **Less parsing.** Since `zTOC.md` is generated, the tool never reads it, except once to migrate an old one. Rung 1's line grammar shrinks to that migration, and the "hand edit" check is just regenerate and compare.

**Effect on the ladder I sketched.** It's the same shape, aimed at a different file:

It's less of a problem than it looks, as long as the change goes forward and doesn't rewrite anything. The two repos record different things:

- **The work-repo records structure.** The cycle's bookmark holds rungs 0 to 2, and new rungs append to it.
- **The agent-repo records time.** It holds the session as it happened, three local commits past `origin`'s `main`, each paired by `ochid:` trailer with its work commit:

  ```
  @  oqvsoolu   (the session since, uncommitted)
  ○  kqklpqom   fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole
  ○  nlvuonlt   fix: the ladder marks done rungs only
  ○  nmxuuvvl   fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current opening
  ◆  lwvzpxzv   feat: improve vc-x1 cycle flow closing   (main@origin)
  ```

The redesign is just one more stretch of the session. It sits in the agent `@` now and goes into the agent half of the next rung's pair, like any other discussion. Nothing already committed on either side becomes wrong: rungs 0 to 2 happened, and the transcript of why the plan changed is the agent-repo's job. The linear agent-repo matches the timeline exactly, and the pairs link by change id, not by position, so the work-repo's ladder can grow without the agent side changing shape.

It turns into a real problem only if we *rewrite* committed work. Each kind of rewrite hits the agent side:

- **Renaming the cycle.** That means re-describing the opening, and every commit is trailer-carrying, which "No re-describe without coordinating" forbids without a coordinated re-describe in both repos. That's the strongest reason to keep the current title, even though it's narrow.
- **Dropping or squashing away rung 2.** Its agent commit's `ochid:` would name a change that no longer exists, and validation would flag it. Keeping rung 2 and noting that rung 5 supersedes it avoids that.
- **Reordering rungs.** It's possible on the work side while local, but the agent commits stay chronological. The links still resolve, so nothing breaks, but the agent history would no longer read in ladder order. Not worth it.
- **The set-aside commit is work-only.** It was a bare `jj commit` with no trailer and no agent pair, so abandoning it touches nothing on the agent side.

So the recipe for this cycle:
1. Keep the title and rungs 0 to 2.
2. Delete `aside-docs-rung` and later abandon its commit.
3. Revise the record's plan and add the new rung headings in `TODO.md`.
4. Carry on. The next rung's pair commits the agent `@`, which holds this whole redesign discussion, so the agent-repo records the turn exactly where it happened.

When rung 3 records change ids in `TODO.md`, those are work-repo ids. The agent side keeps pairing through its trailers, unchanged.

The plain version: the agent-repo is a diary, so changing the plan is just a new entry and needs no special handling. Trouble comes only from rewriting commits already made, like renaming the cycle or deleting a rung, because their agent partners point at them. So we keep what's committed and only add.

content.text:
I agree. It makes the property we just relied on, "keep what's committed and only add", something the tool enforces rather than something we remember. Some thoughts on how it would work.

**How `vc-x1` detects a deletion.** It compares against the last committed record, with no graph inference. Every rung that is `done` or `current` in `@-`'s `TODO.md` must still be in the working copy's `TODO.md`, with the same heading and the same block, though its state may move forward. The set of `done` rungs only grows from commit to commit, and that check is local, cheap, and exact. On a violation, every stage that writes (`--rung-start`, `--commit`, `--close`, `--ladder`) refuses, naming the missing or altered rung and the way back: `jj restore --from @- TODO.md`, or restore just that rung. `--status` reports the violation without refusing, since it changes nothing.

**What exactly is frozen**
- **Frozen:** the heading of a `done` rung, because it's the commit's title and its anchor, and its block (state and change id).
- **Not frozen:** the prose under it. The rung subsection is meant to be revised as the cycle learns, as with this cycle's rung 2, whose subsection will say rung 5 supersedes it.
- **Order:** moving a `done` rung relative to other `done` rungs would contradict the commit order, so I'd refuse that too. Inserting unstarted rungs anywhere stays free.
- **Unstarted rungs:** no block, or `planned`. They're the plan, still freely edited, deleted, or reordered, as now.

**`dead-end` as a state.** It generalizes nicely: today only a whole cycle can be a dead-end (`--close --dead-end`), and this gives a single rung the same honest ending.
- **For a `current` rung with no commit:** `dead-end` records that it was tried. The working copy's edits are reverted or set aside, and the block stays as the record of the attempt.
- **For a `done` rung:** `dead-end` keeps its change id, so its agent partner's `ochid:` still resolves. A later rung reverts the work if needed. The rung was done, and the direction was then abandoned.
- **Back to unmarked:** I'd allow it only for a `current` rung with no commit, as "started by mistake". You said `dead-end` should be the way, so it could also be refused. Your call. I'd lean to allowing it, because no commit exists to protect.
- **The closed record:** `dead-end` rungs show in the ladder as `(dead-end)`, and a closing whose rungs are all `done` or `dead-end` is complete. Today's rationale finding, "a rung reading otherwise is a finding", becomes "a rung neither done nor dead-end is a finding".

**"Start a new cycle, not advised."** `cycle --open` already refuses while a cycle is in progress, so in practice this means closing the current one with `--close --dead-end` first and then opening a fresh one. That path already exists and records everything. Marking rungs `dead-end` inside the cycle is better when the subject survives, as it does here. A dead-end closing is for when the subject itself is abandoned.

**Scope.** Only the `## In Progress` block is protected. The next opening may still delete `## Closed`, since the landmark holds it.

**For this cycle.** Nothing needs to change. Rung 2 stays `done`, the set-aside docs edits belong to a rung that was never started, and the rule becomes a check in rung 3 or 5. I'd put it in rung 5, since it's part of "the record is the cycle's truth". From then on this cycle is protected by it.

The plain version: once a rung is started or done, its heading and state block in `TODO.md` can't be removed or altered, only moved forward, to `done` or `dead-end`. `vc-x1` checks this against the last commit and refuses to go on until it's restored. The explanatory text under each rung stays editable, and abandoning work means marking it `dead-end`, never deleting it.

content.text:
Agreed, and it closes a gap: the rules already say "a ladder lands as a trapezoid" and call linear "the user's to ask for", but the tool does the opposite. A bare `cycle --close --multi-step` makes a linear closing, and you have to add `--trapezoid <target>` to get the default the rules describe.

**`--close` as the only way out of a cycle**
- With the never-delete rule this mostly enforces itself. `cycle --open` already refuses while a cycle is in progress, and deleting the `## In Progress` block would delete its `done` rungs, which the new check refuses. The only way a cycle leaves `## In Progress` is `cycle --close`.
- Not closing stays the user's choice. A cycle can sit open on its local bookmark for as long as you like, and nothing forces a close. The tool only refuses the shortcuts around it.
- A cycle whose subject is abandoned still closes, through `--close --dead-end`. Its started rungs read `done` or `dead-end`, and it lands like any other, as the rules already say.

**Trapezoid as the multi-step default.** The catch is that a trapezoid needs a target, and the rules say the target is "named on the command each time, never assumed". So "default" can't mean the tool silently picks `main`. I'd make it:
- `cycle --close --multi-step --trapezoid <target>`: the default, the form the rules, help, and `--status`'s `next:` line all lead with.
- `cycle --close --multi-step --linear`: the explicit choice for a linear closing.
- A bare `--multi-step` with neither is refused, naming both forms. Nothing is guessed, and linear only happens when someone asks for it, which is what the rule already intends.
- The same applies to `--dead-end` closings, which are multi-step.
- A single-step close has no shape to choose, since it's one commit.

**Effect on this cycle.** It's one more piece of the closing's behaviour, small enough to fold into rung 5 alongside the never-delete check: both are "the tool enforces how a cycle may end". The docs rung then updates the Cycle shape section, which currently says "Without `--trapezoid` the closing is linear". This cycle's own closing would be the first to use the new form.

The plain version: every cycle ends through `cycle --close`, though when is up to you. A multi-step close should be a trapezoid unless you explicitly say `--linear`. Because the target is never assumed, the tool asks you to name either `--trapezoid <target>` or `--linear` instead of quietly picking one.

content.text:
That reads well to me: `--close --dead-end` is the recommended way to abandon a cycle, and `--open` over a cycle in progress is the shortcut, which closes the old cycle as a dead-end instead of refusing. I'm reading "previous commit" as the previous *cycle*. Some points to settle so the shortcut is safe.

**1. The implicit dead-end has to be a real closing commit, not just a marker.** That's the agent-repo point again. The old cycle's rungs have agent partners on the agent `main`, linear and eventually pushed, whose `ochid:` trailers name work commits on the old bookmark. If those work commits never reach `main`, those trailers end up dangling. So `--open` has to do exactly what `--close --multi-step --dead-end` does:
   - mark the `current` rung `dead-end`, leave `done` rungs as they are, and leave unstarted rungs unmarked;
   - move the record to `## Closed` and make the closing commit pair.
   It follows that `--open` then commits, which it never did before, so it needs `-s b` in this case and refuses without it.

**2. Where the new cycle starts.** After the implicit closing, `@` sits on the dead-end's closing commit. I'd have the new cycle stack right there, for three reasons:
   - The target is never assumed, so `--open` can't jump to `main` on its own.
   - Stacking keeps everything landable. Landing the new cycle carries the dead-end cycle's commits with it, so every agent trailer resolves on `main`.
   - It matches how cycles already chain. The dead-end's closing commit is a landmark holding its finished record, and the new opening deletes `## Closed` as usual.

   A user who wants the dead-end landed on its own first can still do that (explicit close, Land, then open).

**3. Why the explicit path stays preferred.** `--close --dead-end` gets a reviewed closing:
   - Its record says what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it.
   - It can close as a trapezoid with a named target.
   - It's landed deliberately.

   The implicit one can only be linear, since no target is named, and only has the default body. So `--open` should say loudly what it did, along the lines of "cycle --open: 'X' was in progress and is closed as a dead-end, linear, on its bookmark, not landed", and `--status` should show it the way it shows any closed, unlanded cycle.

**4. What the shortcut leaves to the user.**
   - The new rule still protects the old cycle's `done` rungs: they move to `## Closed` intact and are never deleted.
   - The dead-end's record has no "what was tried" prose unless the user writes it. A finding in `--status`, saying the dead-end closing has the default body, would nudge them.

**Effect on this cycle.** It's more closing behaviour: `--open` learning to perform the dead-end closing. It fits rung 5 with the other "how a cycle may end" rules, though rung 5 is getting large. I'd split it: rung 5 for the record as the source of truth (change ids, the never-delete check), and a new rung 6, **feat: a cycle ends by --close, and --open closes a dead-end**, covering the trapezoid-or-`--linear` choice and the implicit dead-end. The docs rung and closing follow as 7 and 8.

The plain version: the advice is to end a cycle you're abandoning with `cycle --close --dead-end`. If someone just runs `cycle --open` instead, the tool closes the old cycle as a dead-end for them, with a real commit so nothing it pointed to is lost, then starts the new cycle on top of it and tells them clearly what it did. The new rung for this lands in the plan just before the docs rung.

# Notes file conventions

Conventions the agent follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, and the frozen `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and
`notes/done.md`, [Frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done)). One source of truth lives here,
and [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this before editing a notes file.

## File reads: read the slice you need

Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs. Grep or read
further on demand ([why](rationale.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).

- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In Progress` +
  the top of `## Todo`, its entries in priority order. `Read` with `offset=0, limit=60`.
  `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`. Read further only when chasing a lower entry, an Idea, a
  `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below `## Todo`). Read
  only when picking up a backlog item, and grep to locate it first.
- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small, so read it whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
  `## Bugs` pointer in `TODO.md`.
- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: frozen history. Scan headings first
  (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you need.

## Notes references

Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]` for
several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay single-bracketed.

## Reference numbering

Every note file keeps a file-local `# References` section at the bottom, and its numbers are scoped
to that file: the same `[1]` in two files is two independent slots, each pointing wherever its own
file defines.

- Treat `[N]` as a **footnote**, a slot meaningful only inside its own file's `# References`, so a
  citation never reuses another file's number. To cite a target a sibling file references, take your
  own next free slot and define it, and the same target may carry a different number in each file.
- A `[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is a quoted identifier, data rather than a citation,
  so it needs no definition.
- To point at a section of another file, use an inline link with an anchor rather than a bare
  number.
- A definition is usually a path with an anchor, and may also be a **same-file fragment**,
  `[N]: #<slug>`, which is how a ladder rung links its own subsection ([The In Progress
  block](#the-in-progress-block)).
- A file's `# References` may be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in first-citation order,
  walking the file's prose top to bottom. A file-local rewrite: no other file moves, and a new ref
  may take the next free number, out of order being fine. Ask before re-packing, and never re-pack
  [frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done).

## Markdown anchor links

GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining spaces
to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b` (spaces on both
sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General markdown reference:
[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no official spec for
auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).

## Todo format

`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
reference links to more detail.

- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
- `## Ideas`: unranked.
- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
  numbering](#reference-numbering)).

Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
project's record, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.

An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
bold title, cited by the bold text.

Example shape:

```
## Todo

### Add new feature X

The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).

### Fix bug Y

What is wrong and where [[1]].

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
```

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **rungs**: a `#### Rungs` heading over the rung subsections, the ladder itself being `zTOC.md`'s
  ([zTOC format](#ztoc-format)), made by the tool from the subsections' headings, so a rung is
  written once, as its heading: one rung per step, `- 2 (done) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`: the
  rung's number, its position in the ladder from `0`, then the marker, `(done)` or `(current)`,
  both first so they read down their columns, and a rung not yet started has neither, and an inline
  link so the ladder is one list with nothing beside it to keep in step, its line as long as the
  title makes it. A rung is `(done)` when a commit of its title is on the cycle's branch and
  `(current)` when it is the first without one, so no marker is typed. `<title>` is the rung's
  commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per [Conventional-commit
  shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a `## Todo` entry is retitled as
  its cycle title before `cycle --open` moves it. The first rung is `<cycle title> opening` and the
  last `<cycle title> closing`, linked like the rest

`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
`_None._`.

A rung is `- N (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title
links to the rung's subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- N (marker) <cycle title>`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## zTOC format

`zTOC.md`, beside `TODO.md` at the work-repo root, is the workspace's index, so the running ladder
and the files worth knowing are found without reading `TODO.md`'s length, and the `z` sorts it last
in a listing. Its sections, in this order:

- `# TOC`, the title.
- `## Ladder`: the cycle's ladder, its one copy, each rung with its marker as [The In Progress
  block](#the-in-progress-block) shapes it, linking across to its subsection in `TODO.md`, since a
  same-file link does not work in every markdown preview, zed's among them. Written by `vc-x1
  cycle --open`, replacing the last cycle's, made again from the rung headings by `cycle --ladder`
  and by every cycle commit, and kept by the closing commit, so the landmark's tree holds the
  finished ladder beside its `## Closed`. Its grammar is strict: each rung a left-margin `- `
  line, and the tool refuses to rewrite a ladder holding any other line but a blank one.
- `## The TOC`: one link per file worth knowing, with what it holds, `TODO.md` first.

Its links are inline, so it has no `# References`.

Like `TODO.md` it is not an agent-file, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton, `##
Ladder` reading `_None._` until the first opening.

## Frozen history: chores and done

`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
They are frozen: nothing is appended, no section is opened, no entry is retired into them, and no
ref is backfilled. They stay in place because Todo entries and design notes link into them, and
those links stay valid. Read them as history, by the slice you need.

124	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
125	- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
126	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
127	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
128	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
129	  answer
130	- **rungs**: a `#### Rungs` heading over the rung subsections, the ladder itself being `zTOC.md`'s
131	  ([zTOC format](#ztoc-format)), made by the tool from the subsections' headings, so a rung is
132	  written once, as its heading: one rung per step, `- 2 (done) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`: the
133	  rung's number, its position in the ladder from `0`, then the marker, `(done)` or `(current)`,
134	  both first so they read down their columns, and a rung not yet started has neither, and an inline
135	  link so the ladder is one list with nothing beside it to keep in step, its line as long as the
136	  title makes it. A rung is `(done)` when a commit of its title is on the cycle's branch and
137	  `(current)` when it is the first without one, so no marker is typed. `<title>` is the rung's
138	  commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per [Conventional-commit
139	  shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a `## Todo` entry is retitled as
140	  its cycle title before `cycle --open` moves it. The first rung is `<cycle title> opening` and the
141	  last `<cycle title> closing`, linked like the rest
142	
143	`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
144	included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
145	with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
146	completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
147	never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
148	the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
149	`_None._`.
150	
151	A rung is `- N (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title
152	links to the rung's subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
153	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
154	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
155	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
156	
157	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- N (marker) <cycle title>`, with no subsection
158	under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
159	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
160	
161	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
162	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
163	
164	## zTOC format
165	
166	`zTOC.md`, beside `TODO.md` at the work-repo root, is the workspace's index, so the running ladder
167	and the files worth knowing are found without reading `TODO.md`'s length, and the `z` sorts it last
168	in a listing. Its sections, in this order:
169	
170	- `# TOC`, the title.
171	- `## Ladder`: the cycle's ladder, its one copy, each rung with its marker as [The In Progress
172	  block](#the-in-progress-block) shapes it, linking across to its subsection in `TODO.md`, since a
173	  same-file link does not work in every markdown preview, zed's among them. Written by `vc-x1
174	  cycle --open`, replacing the last cycle's, made again from the rung headings by `cycle --ladder`
175	  and by every cycle commit, and kept by the closing commit, so the landmark's tree holds the
176	  finished ladder beside its `## Closed`. Its grammar is strict: each rung a left-margin `- `
177	  line, and the tool refuses to rewrite a ladder holding any other line but a blank one.
178	- `## The TOC`: one link per file worth knowing, with what it holds, `TODO.md` first.
179	
180	Its links are inline, so it has no `# References`.
181	
182	Like `TODO.md` it is not an agent-file, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton, `##
183	Ladder` reading `_None._` until the first opening.
184	
185	## Frozen history: chores and done
186	
187	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
188	cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
189	They are frozen: nothing is appended, no section is opened, no entry is retired into them, and no
190	ref is backfilled. They stay in place because Todo entries and design notes link into them, and
191	those links stay valid. Read them as history, by the slice you need.
192	
</system-reminder>

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules.
